purpose: A reviewable leaf registry derived from the Mathematics pilot tree.

atomicity_contract.definition: Atomicity is operational: a leaf is small enough to classify and review independently, but may contain many concepts, methods, and applications.
atomicity_contract.review_state_note: machine_validated means JSON and internal references passed checks; it is not human approval.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of vector spaces, subspaces, bases, dimension, linear maps, kernels, images, and canonical linear constructions.
scope_excludes: Nonlinear maps as the primary object
atomicity_reasons: The objects and morphisms form one coherent algebraic scope.
Its boundary can be tested without importing matrix-specific or nonlinear topics.
It is a stable independent review target in linear algebra.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Include statements about vector spaces, subspaces, bases, dimension, and linear maps; route matrix-specific canonical-form work to Matrix Theory.
review_notes: Check whether modules should be included or deferred to a later expansion.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of matrices, determinants, canonical forms, eigenstructure, matrix decompositions, and matrix invariants.
scope_excludes: Numerical linear algebra software engineering
atomicity_reasons: Matrix objects provide a coherent algebraic boundary.
Matrix theory has recognizable questions and literature.
It can be reviewed separately from abstract vector-space language.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Include matrix invariants and canonical forms; route abstract linear-map statements without matrix representation to Vector Spaces and Linear Maps.
review_notes: Check overlap with numerical linear algebra before dataset use.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of existence, uniqueness, structure, and solution methods for systems of linear equations and related operator equations.
scope_excludes: Nonlinear differential equation solving
atomicity_reasons: The target question is unified by linear solvability.
The inclusion and exclusion boundary is concrete.
It is a useful leaf for elementary and applied classification examples.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Include linear equation systems and their solution spaces; exclude nonlinear systems and numerical implementation details.
review_notes: Decide whether this leaf remains separate from Matrix Theory for the intended dataset behavior.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of divisibility, congruences, primes, arithmetic functions, and integer properties using elementary or classical methods.
scope_excludes: Number fields as the primary framework
atomicity_reasons: It is unified by classical arithmetic questions about integers.
Its boundary is recognizable through elementary divisibility and congruence methods.
It is an independent teaching and review target.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Include integer divisibility, congruence, and primes; route number fields and ideals to Algebraic Number Theory.
review_notes: Verify the Arabic label against project terminology.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of algebraic numbers, number fields, ideals, valuations, and arithmetic properties of algebraic extensions.
scope_excludes: General abstract algebra without arithmetic focus
atomicity_reasons: Number fields and their arithmetic form one coherent object family.
The boundary is stable through algebraic-number terminology.
It is independently reviewable at research-subfield level.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Include arithmetic of number fields and ideals; exclude abstract algebra without a number-theoretic question.
review_notes: Check whether algebraic geometry cross-links are needed in the later graph layer.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of arithmetic questions using analytic functions, complex analysis, asymptotic methods, and estimates.
scope_excludes: Real analysis without arithmetic questions
atomicity_reasons: The leaf is unified by analytic methods applied to arithmetic.
Its boundary separates arithmetic questions from general analysis.
It is a recognizable research subfield.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require an arithmetic target such as primes or L-functions; otherwise route to the relevant Analysis leaf.
review_notes: Review placement under Number Theory versus a cross-domain Analysis link.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of polynomial or related equations whose solutions are sought in integers, rational numbers, or other arithmetic domains.
scope_excludes: Numerical root finding over the reals
atomicity_reasons: The solution-domain constraint gives a coherent boundary.
It has stable problem forms and recognizable methods.
It is useful as a separate classification target for arithmetic problems.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require an arithmetic domain for solutions; exclude ordinary real or complex root finding.
review_notes: Check whether arithmetic geometry examples should be deferred to crosswalks.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of rates of change, derivatives, local approximation, extrema, and differential behavior of functions.
scope_excludes: Integration as the primary operation
atomicity_reasons: The derivative and local-change questions are coherent.
Its boundary can be tested by the primary operation and goal.
It is independently useful for educational and applied classification.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Route accumulation-first questions to Integral Calculus and manifold-first questions to Differential Geometry.
review_notes: Confirm level is sufficiently broad for a leaf rather than a single technique.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of accumulation, definite and indefinite integrals, integration theorems, and quantities obtained by integration.
scope_excludes: Measure theory in its full generality
atomicity_reasons: Accumulation and integration provide one coherent scope.
Its boundary is clear against differentiation and full measure theory.
It is a stable independent review target.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Route derivative-first questions to Differential Calculus and measure-theoretic questions beyond elementary integration to Analysis.
review_notes: Review the treatment of Lebesgue integration in future expansions.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of limits, derivatives, integrals, and optimization for functions of several real variables.
scope_excludes: Abstract manifold theory as the primary setting
atomicity_reasons: Several-variable functions provide a coherent setting.
The boundary is recognizable by coordinates and partial/multiple operations.
It is a practical independent review target.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Route smooth-manifold structure to Differential Geometry and one-variable fundamentals to Differential or Integral Calculus.
review_notes: Decide whether vector calculus should be a sibling leaf or a cross-linked specialization.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of scalar and vector fields, line and surface integrals, and differential operators in Euclidean spaces.
scope_excludes: General vector space theory without calculus
atomicity_reasons: Field operators and integral theorems form one coherent package.
The boundary separates calculus on fields from abstract linear algebra.
It is a stable target for mathematical modeling examples.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require a vector/scalar field or line/surface operation; route abstract vector spaces to Linear Algebra.
review_notes: Review whether its primary parent should be Analysis or Geometry in a multi-parent graph.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The axioms, events, sigma-algebras, probability measures, conditional probability, and independence underlying probability theory.
scope_excludes: Statistical estimation from observed samples
atomicity_reasons: Axiomatic probability objects form a coherent foundation.
The boundary is explicit against inference and data analysis.
It is independently reviewable as a mathematical target.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Include probability spaces and measure-level definitions; route sample-based estimation to Statistical Inference.
review_notes: Confirm whether measure-theoretic probability needs a separate future leaf.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of random variables, probability distributions, expectations, moments, dependence, and transformations.
scope_excludes: Time-indexed stochastic evolution as the primary object
atomicity_reasons: Random variables and distributions share a stable object-level boundary.
The leaf is distinct from axiomatic foundations and time-indexed processes.
It is a useful target for basic probability classification.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Route time-indexed dependence to Stochastic Processes and data-based estimation to Statistics.
review_notes: Review the scope of distribution families in later dataset examples.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of random processes indexed by time or another parameter, including dependence, paths, and long-run behavior.
scope_excludes: Static distributions without an indexing process
atomicity_reasons: Indexing and path behavior give a coherent boundary.
It has established subfield terminology and methods.
It can be reviewed independently from static probability.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require a random process indexed by time or another parameter; exclude single random variables.
review_notes: Check whether stochastic differential equations are deferred to a future crosswalk.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of estimating unknown quantities, testing hypotheses, and quantifying uncertainty from data under statistical models.
scope_excludes: Descriptive summaries without inference
atomicity_reasons: Inference tasks share a data-to-uncertainty objective.
The boundary is clear against description and data collection.
It is a stable central statistics review target.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require a model-based claim about unknown quantities or hypotheses; route prediction-specific models to Regression Analysis when appropriate.
review_notes: Review the overlap between frequentist and Bayesian inference leaves.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of conditional relationships and prediction using regression models, including linear and generalized models.
scope_excludes: Machine-learning engineering outside statistical modeling
atomicity_reasons: Conditional modeling and prediction form a coherent scope.
The boundary is testable through the presence of a response-predictor relationship.
It is a stable statistics review target.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require a regression relationship; route general estimation without a regression structure to Statistical Inference.
review_notes: Mark ML-specific examples as cross-domain rather than silently expanding this leaf.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of principled assignment, control, randomization, and analysis plans for learning causal or comparative information from experiments.
scope_excludes: Laboratory operations without a statistical design question
atomicity_reasons: Assignment and control decisions define one coherent statistical scope.
Its boundary is clear against laboratory operations.
It is an independent review target for causal study design.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require a statistical design or assignment question; exclude operational experiment execution.
review_notes: Review whether observational study design should be included later.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of statistical reasoning that combines prior distributions with likelihoods to obtain posterior uncertainty and decisions.
scope_excludes: Philosophical debate about probability without statistical modeling
atomicity_reasons: Prior-likelihood-posterior reasoning gives a coherent boundary.
It has distinct vocabulary and inferential workflow.
It is independently reviewable without making all Statistics Bayesian.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require Bayesian updating or decision structure; route non-Bayesian inference to Statistical Inference.
review_notes: Review whether the leaf is too method-oriented for the project's final taxonomy.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of counting finite structures, generating functions, recurrence relations, and exact enumeration methods.
scope_excludes: Continuous probability distributions
atomicity_reasons: Exact counting and generating methods form one coherent scope.
The boundary is testable through finite enumeration goals.
It is a recognizable combinatorics review target.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require counting or enumeration of finite structures; route extremal objectives to Extremal Combinatorics.
review_notes: Check whether generating functions require a separate cross-domain relation to Analysis.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of maximum or minimum size and structure of finite configurations subject to combinatorial constraints.
scope_excludes: Continuous optimization without a finite combinatorial structure
atomicity_reasons: Optimization of finite structure under constraints gives a coherent target.
Its extremal objective distinguishes it from pure enumeration.
It is independently useful for problem classification.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require a finite combinatorial object and an extremal size or forbidden-structure question.
review_notes: Review overlap with Structural Graph Theory for graph-specific examples.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of graph structure through connectivity, minors, decompositions, coloring, cycles, and structural invariants.
scope_excludes: Operational network monitoring
atomicity_reasons: Graph structure and invariants provide one coherent mathematical scope.
The boundary is stable against operational networking.
It is an independent graph-theory review target.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require a structural property or graph class; route algorithmic procedure emphasis to Graph Algorithms.
review_notes: Check whether extremal graph questions should cross-link to Extremal Combinatorics.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of algorithms whose inputs, outputs, or correctness properties are expressed using graph structures.
scope_excludes: General software engineering practices
atomicity_reasons: Graph-structured algorithmic problems form a coherent target.
The cross-domain boundary is explicitly recorded rather than hidden.
It is useful for testing classification of mathematical and computational examples.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require graph structure in the formal problem; route general algorithms without graph structure outside this Mathematics pilot.
review_notes: Human reviewer must decide whether this remains in Mathematics or moves to a cross-domain view.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of sets, membership, cardinality, ordinal structure, axioms, and constructions used as mathematical foundations.
scope_excludes: Database set operations as an implementation topic
atomicity_reasons: Sets and foundational constructions form a coherent object language.
The boundary is explicit against application-level set operations.
It is a stable independent foundations review target.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require mathematical set-theoretic objects, axioms, or cardinal/ordinal reasoning.
review_notes: Review whether Foundations should be a sibling discipline in a future wider tree.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of which functions and problems can be computed, with what resources, and by which formal models of computation.
scope_excludes: Application programming and software delivery
atomicity_reasons: Formal computability and undecidability form one coherent mathematical scope.
Its boundary excludes software delivery explicitly.
It is a recognized logic and foundations review target.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require a formal computability or decidability question; exclude implementation performance alone.
review_notes: Review cross-domain links to theoretical computer science before expansion.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of formal proofs as mathematical objects, including proof systems, consistency, normalization, and proof strength.
scope_excludes: Informal proof-writing advice
atomicity_reasons: Formal proofs and proof systems form one object-level scope.
The boundary separates proof theory from informal pedagogy.
It is independently reviewable within mathematical logic.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require formal proof objects or proof-system properties; exclude general advice on writing proofs.
review_notes: Review relation to Foundations if a separate discipline is introduced.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of classical Euclidean figures and theorems involving incidence, congruence, similarity, angles, circles, and metric relations.
scope_excludes: Coordinate methods as the primary representation
atomicity_reasons: Classical figures and metric/incidence theorems form a coherent scope.
The boundary is clear against coordinate and smooth methods.
It is independently reviewable for elementary geometry.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Prefer synthetic or metric Euclidean reasoning; route coordinate-first problems to Coordinate Geometry.
review_notes: Confirm whether one leaf is sufficient for the pilot's geometry examples.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of geometric figures and relations represented by coordinates, equations, vectors, and transformations in Euclidean spaces.
scope_excludes: Abstract algebraic varieties
atomicity_reasons: Coordinates and equations provide one coherent representation.
Its boundary is testable by the explicit use of coordinate methods.
It is a practical independent classification leaf.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require coordinates, equations, or coordinate transformations as the primary method.
review_notes: Review overlap with elementary algebra and analytic geometry curricula.

atomic_disciplines.definition: The study of smooth curves and surfaces through parametrization, curvature, tangent spaces, metrics, and local or global geometric properties.
scope_excludes: Elementary plane geometry without smooth structure
atomicity_reasons: Smooth curves and surfaces form a coherent geometric object family.
The boundary is explicit through smooth structure and curvature.
It is an independent entry point to differential geometry.
atomic_disciplines.boundary_test: Require a smooth curve or surface and a differential-geometric property; exclude purely elementary figures.
review_notes: Decide whether manifolds need a separate leaf in a later version.
